reason: The first 704-proposal finite audit gave the observer both unmasked initial-tree outputs and row-wise predictions of the refitted reference anchor on the outer sample. This sensitivity removes these extra observations and evaluates the reference and reduced metrics together under each assignment. It is a retrospective follow-up to that result.
observable: Hold all development data, proposal-row transcripts and labels, model fits, outer labels and the multiset of complete outer feature vectors fixed. For the actual pre-refit observer add no row-wise outer outputs. For two intermediate observers add the frozen candidate/anchor outputs on the outer rows for (a) the empty restoration, or (b) all recorded restorations, respectively. A final reference fit's outer scores are hidden in all three cases. Distinct feature rows remain complete and may exchange positions only within each observed transcript class.
passing: Score the same row permutation for both the original reduced refit and separately refitted anchor. Check the actual 3% pairwise relative metric floors for AUC and accuracy. Known fixed score multisets ensure both accuracy and rank-sum AUC gaps are linear in assignment. Retain a concrete permutation and both recomputed metric pairs for each opposite decision.
computation: Optimize each gap in both directions. Within classes of at most 48 rows optimize without blocking. For larger classes initially search only permutations within contiguous blocks of at most 48 rows in original row order, without looking at their labels or scores to make blocks. These are valid witnesses, not full-orbit bounds. Report the number with a counterexample, number with provably unchanged decisions (only for unrestricted classes or pointwise identical refit and anchor), and number unresolved separately. All results conditional on these 704 proposals; no frequency claim on independent naturally occurring test panels.
